images.caption: Figure 1:Attention distributions across ViT layers.Shallow layers show dispersed attention over edges and textures; deeper layers progressively concentrate on a few semantic anchors.

Figure 3:Overview ofDGP.(A) At every LLM layer, the Dynamic Gated Pathways module routes overallViT layers conditioned on the current language-layer state, aggregates the selected visual features, and injects them back into the LLM hidden states through a gated residual connection—establishing all-to-all cross-layer connections between ViT and LLM. (B) Inside the module, ViT layer summaries serve as keys/values and the language-layer state as the query; a shared cross-attention followed by a layer-specific routing MLP produces the per-layer routing weights.Weight Matrix(m)denotes the routing weights of LLM layermmover all ViT layers.

Figure 4:Qualitative comparison betweenDGPand LLaVA-1.5.Representative examples from math solving, OCR understanding, and detailed visual reasoning. LLaVA-1.5 often misses critical visual evidence or hallucinates content;DGPproduces more accurate, evidence-grounded responses by adaptively accessing multi-granularity visual features.

Figure 5:Gated Pathway Analysis.(A) Heatmap of routing weights over LLM (x) and ViT (y) layers. (B) Routing curves of representative LLM layers with multimodal patterns. (C) Routing weights of LLM layer 21 across benchmarks, showing task-specific preferences. (D) Per-sample routing distributions within the same benchmark, showing sample-level diversity.
Figure 6:Task-aware routing for the same image.As the question changes, routing shifts: attribute recognition activates shallower layers, while global-semantic questions activate deeper ones.
Figure 7:Fused visual feature visualization.We compare CLIP layer 23, the uniform average over all 24 ViT layers, andDGP’s gated fusion at different LLM layers.
